title: Can SAEs Detect Emergent Misalignment from Fine-Tuning? Replicating and Extending OpenAI's Result

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong: prospective detection of fine-tuning-induced misalignment is a direct safety application. Replicating with open-source models makes the finding generalizable and verifiable. High practical relevance.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: fine-tuning small models (Phi-2, Gemma-2-2B) is well-documented. SAELens provides pre-trained SAEs. Comparing feature activation distributions before/after is standard analysis. Achievable with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused: fine-tune model on narrow misbehavior, compare SAE features before/after, train detection probe. Clear protocol with well-defined deliverable. Achievable in 30 hours with medium compute.

novelty.reasoning: OpenAI published the original work, it was replicated on open-weight models with released code and SAEs, and Nature validated the phenomenon. The proposed replication is redundant.

evidence.source: OpenAI - Debugging misaligned completions with SAE latent attribution (2025)
evidence.finding: OpenAI directly uses SAE latent attribution to debug misaligned completions, comparing models before and after problematic fine-tuning to identify misalignment-associated features.

evidence.source: OpenAI - Persona Features Control Emergent Misalignment (2025)
evidence.finding: Identifies 'misaligned persona' features via SAEs that can detect misalignment with as little as 5% incorrect training data, before behavioral evaluations show any misalignment.

evidence.source: LessWrong - Finding misaligned persona features in open-weight models (2025)
evidence.finding: Already replicates the approach on open-weight models (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) using BatchTopK SAEs, with released code and SAEs.

evidence.source: OpenAI - Helpful assistant features suppress emergent misalignment (2025)
evidence.finding: Extends the SAE misalignment detection work to show that helpful assistant features actively suppress emergent misalignment, deepening the mechanistic understanding.

evidence.source: Nature (2025) - Fine-tuning on narrow tasks leads to broad misalignment
evidence.finding: Published in Nature, demonstrating that fine-tuning LLMs on narrow tasks like writing insecure code causes broad misalignment across unrelated domains.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: This is largely addressed. OpenAI published the original SAE-based misalignment detection work in 2025. The open-source replication has already been done (LessWrong post with Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B, with released code and SAEs). The Nature publication validates the broad misalignment phenomenon. The proposed work is essentially a re-replication of already-replicated results.
